summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for abdominal pain localized around her gastrostomy tube site, worsening over three days. She has a complex history including prior gastric bypass and reversal, post-surgical hypoglycemia, and multiple prior admissions for similar pain. Management was conservative: tube feeds were held and IV dextrose was given to prevent hypoglycemia. Pain improved with this approach. Oral intake was initially poor, so Marinol was started, which significantly improved caloric intake to 90% of goal. The patient tolerated gradual reintroduction of tube feeds without pain recurrence. She was discharged home after 15 days, pain-free and stable, with a plan to follow up with her surgeon and dietitian. The long-term goal is to discontinue tube feeds if oral intake remains adequate and symptoms do not return.
